Miniamin
mĭn´ĭ-ă-mĭn
n. (a Levite under Hezekiah; also a priestly house after the exile)
Hebrew Minyamin, a shortened form of Benjamin, son of the right hand. The name belongs to a Levite trusted with distribution under Hezekiah and to a priestly course after the return.

Biblical Definition

Hezekiah's reformation produced such a quantity of tithes and offerings that a distribution system had to be built, and this man was one of those trusted with it: “And next him were Eden, and Miniamin, and Jeshua, and Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in their set office, to give to their brethren by courses, as well to the great as to the small” (2 Chronicles 31:15). The clause as well to the great as to the small is the standard the whole arrangement was held to. A priestly house of the name returns in Nehemiah's register: “Of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai” (Nehemiah 12:17). And at the dedication of the wall a priest of the name blows a trumpet in the great procession: “And the priests; Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Michaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets” (Nehemiah 12:41). The reason there was anything to distribute in Hezekiah's day is given a few verses earlier: “And as soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Israel brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field; and the tithe of all things brought they in abundantly” (2 Chronicles 31:5).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Miniamin; the name is a form of Benjamin, and belongs to a Levite under Hezekiah and to a priestly house.

expand to see more

MINIAMIN, n. A Levite in the reign of Hezekiah, set over the distribution of the offerings.

TITHE, n. The tenth part of the increase annually arising from the profits of land and stock, allotted to the clergy.

FIRSTFRUITS, n. The fruit or produce first matured and collected in any season, offered to God.

DISTRIBUTION, n. The act of dividing among a number; dispensation; the dealing out to several persons.

IMPARTIAL, a. Not partial; not biased in favor of one party more than another; equitable; just.

Modern Corruption

Giving is treated as a private transaction with no accounting attached, when Scripture names the men who handled the offerings and records the rule they distributed by.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the care Scripture takes over money given to God. Hezekiah did not simply receive the offerings; he appointed chambers, prepared them, set Conaniah over them with his brother Shimei as second, and named ten men including Miniamin who were in their set office to give to their brethren by courses. Paul does the same thing with the collection for Jerusalem, travelling with appointed men and stating his reason: providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

The standard the Chronicler records is worth more than the administrative detail: as well to the great as to the small. Distribution was by course and by need, and rank did not alter the portion. James says a congregation that seats a man with a gold ring better than a poor man in vile raiment has become a judge with evil thoughts. Where offerings are handled without accounting, or distributed with respect of persons, the church has departed from a pattern the Old Testament laid down in careful prose and named the responsible men in.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Minyamin (H4509), from Benjamin, son of the right hand; maaser (H4643), a tithe; bikkurim (H1061), firstfruits; emunah (H530), faithfulness in office.

expand to see more

Hebrew Minyamin (H4509) — a form of Benjamin, son of the right hand.

Hebrew maaser (H4643) — a tithe, the tenth part.

Hebrew bikkurim (H1061) — firstfruits; brought in abundantly under Hezekiah.

Hebrew machaloqoth (H4256) — courses; to give to their brethren by courses.

Hebrew emunah (H530) — faithfulness; their set office, held in trust.

Usage

"“Eden, and Miniamin, and Jeshua…in their set office” — the distributors."

"“As well to the great as to the small” — the rule of distribution."

"“Miniamin, Michaiah…with trumpets” — at the dedication of the wall."
